meta.title: Dead Before Dawn

victim.name: BrijMohan Valentine
victim.description: Charming, controlling host whose family owns the cabin. He kept a quiet tally of what everyone owed him, in money and in secrets.

meta.tone: claustrophobic cabin-in-the-woods dread, Until Dawn horror, creaking dark and long silences
meta.premise: Five friends come to a secluded cabin in the woods. One of them is found dead in the basement cellar, and one of the others was caught sleeping with the victim's sister and the victim's girlfriend. The rest must find the killer before help arrives.

suspects.name: Rafe Kincaid
suspects.description: Brij's oldest friend and favourite rival. Easy grin, worse decisions. Caught tonight with Brij's sister, and weeks ago with his girlfriend.
suspects.public_alibi: Says he spent that hour locked in the upstairs bathroom, sick on whiskey. Nobody saw him come out.
suspects.motive: Brij caught him with Tara and with Kiara, and swore at dinner to ruin him.

suspects.name: Tara Valentine
suspects.description: Brij's younger sister. Sharp, sleepless and finished with living in his shadow.
suspects.public_alibi: Smoked on the porch with Jonah, watching the treeline, the whole hour.
suspects.motive: Brij caught her with Rafe and threatened to tell their father, who still pays her rent.

suspects.name: Kiara Sol
suspects.description: Brij's girlfriend of three years. Brittle smile, ring finger bare since dinner.
suspects.public_alibi: Packing upstairs to leave at first light. Her footsteps creaked overhead the whole time.
suspects.motive: Brij read her messages to Rafe aloud at the dinner table and laughed.

suspects.name: Jonah Pike
suspects.description: Brij's best friend and business partner. Soft voice, steady hands, the one who drove everyone up here.
suspects.public_alibi: Smoked on the porch with Tara, watching the treeline, the whole hour.
suspects.motive: Takes full control of the company they built together if Brij is gone.

world.killer_method: Just after one in the morning Jonah told Tara he was going to check the generator. He followed Brij down to the cellar, where Brij had gone to confront him about the missing money, and struck him from behind with the fire iron he had carried from the hearth. He laid Brij at the foot of the steps to look like a fall, wiped the iron, hung it back by the fire and switched the generator off by hand so the cellar stayed dark. Motive: Jonah had drained their company for two years, Brij had found the proof, and he meant to hand it to the police at dawn.

clues.text: Brij's phone lies face down in the cellar with one unsent message: 'Jonah. I know about the money. Cellar. Now.'
Tara admits Jonah left the porch to check the generator and was gone long enough for two cigarettes to burn down.
The fire iron hangs by the hearth, wiped too clean. In the ash beneath it is the print of a heavy work boot. Only Jonah wears work boots.
The generator was switched off by hand, not tripped. The lever is smeared with the same red cellar clay caked on Jonah's boots.
In Jonah's coat pocket: a torn strip of ledger paper in Brij's handwriting, the word 'Jonah' underlined twice.
Rafe's belt lies coiled on the cellar steps, and his whiskey glass stands on the shelf right beside the body.

items.name: Brij's ledger
items.description: The company ledger Brij hid behind the cellar boiler. Two years of missing money, every line initialled by the same hand.

items.name: Brass lighter
items.description: Brij's heavy brass lighter. Its small flame keeps the dark back, and somehow keeps your nerve steady too.

on_success.narration: Every initial, every missing month, every lie of the night lines up behind one name. Nobody argues.

on_failure.narration: The name comes out, but the proof slips from shaking hands and scatters across the floor.

solved.title: First Light
solved.epilogue: The ledger lies open on the kitchen table when the police come in, and nobody has to explain it. {killer} does not run; there is nowhere left to go. The money, the cellar, the fire iron wiped too clean, all of it comes out in the grey morning. {survivors} walk out into the cold, alive and changed. {victim} is carried up the cellar steps at last.

wrong_culprit.title: The Wrong Monster
wrong_culprit.epilogue: Rafe is led to the car in the rain, still saying he only wanted a drink in the cellar. The group watches him go and feels nothing like relief. {killer} stands with the others, coat buttoned, face composed for grief. {survivors} will tell the story of that night for years and never once get it right. {victim} deserved the truth, and got a scapegoat.

culprit_escapes.title: Nothing at Dawn
culprit_escapes.epilogue: The police find a fall down the cellar steps, a houseful of exhausted friends and no proof of anything. {killer} drives home alone and parks in the same space as always. {survivors} stop answering each other's messages within a month. {victim}'s cabin goes up for sale, cellar and all. Some nights you still hear something on the steps.
culprit_escapes.epilogue_if_downgraded: The proof was in your hands and the name was on your tongue, and in the last second it all came apart. {killer} walked out to the police car as a witness, not a suspect. {survivors} will relive that one wasted moment for the rest of their lives. {victim}'s ledger went into an evidence bag nobody ever reopened.
